picks.bear: Already up roughly 385% in a year and slipped from about $931 to $877 in late October. Memory is a boom-bust business, and an AI capex pullback would hit it hard.
picks.catalyst: AI capex commentary from this week's big-tech earnings; next Micron report in December.
picks.name: Micron Technology
picks.social: Top-5 on r/wallstreetbets mention trackers this week; mostly bullish.
picks.thesis: Memory for AI data centers is sold out for the year ahead and revenue has grown several-fold year over year. Shows up on nearly every November screen (Forbes, WallStreetZen) and 16 of 24 analysts rate it Strong Buy.

picks.bear: Led last week's tech sell-off as investors questioned AI spending; momentum is below short-term averages.
picks.catalyst: AMD earnings this week as a read-through; Nvidia reports later in November.
picks.name: Nvidia
picks.social: Bullish on WSB trackers, though mention volume is down from peak.
picks.thesis: Morgan Stanley reiterated Buy with a $300 target after GTC Berlin, about 45% above the recent price. Still the core AI infrastructure name.

picks.bear: The miss came from heavy AI capex and weak free cash flow; the market may keep punishing spenders until returns show up.
picks.catalyst: Any stabilization in the AI-capex debate; general tech rebound.
picks.name: Alphabet
picks.social: #1 on ApeWisdom and AltIndex WSB lists, sentiment bullish.
picks.thesis: Fell about 10% after a Q3 profit miss even though Cloud was strong. The most-discussed ticker on WSB this week, with bullish dip-buy sentiment.

picks.bear: Premium valuation; software multiples compress quickly in risk-off weeks.
picks.catalyst: Upgrade momentum; earnings in early December.
picks.name: CrowdStrike
picks.thesis: Deutsche Bank upgraded to Buy today and raised its target to $300 from $240, arguing AI widens the cybersecurity market. Also on Motley Fool's buy-and-hold list.

picks.bear: Reports Nov 4. A miss in a fragile tape could mean a sharp one-day drop.
picks.name: Datadog
picks.thesis: Named a top pick by a highly ranked analyst; cloud migration and AI adoption are driving customer growth.

picks.bear: Revenue growth has slowed four quarters straight, from 18% to 12%. Falling knives can keep falling.
picks.catalyst: No scheduled event this week; a base-building story.
picks.name: Netflix
picks.social: Mixed; value crowd buying, momentum crowd avoiding.
picks.thesis: About 52% below its high and down roughly a third this year; analysts still expect about 20% earnings growth, and Motley Fool argues the slowdown is priced in.

picks.bear: Reports after the close today. Very high valuation means even a good quarter can sell off.
picks.name: Palantir
picks.social: Perennial WSB favorite; heavy options activity into earnings.
picks.thesis: Strong government and commercial AI demand; a beat can spark a big squeeze.

picks.bear: AI-capex worry hit chips hard last week; guidance will be judged harshly.
picks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
picks.thesis: Second-source AI GPUs and data-center CPUs; one of the most anticipated reports this week.

picks.bear: Down about 10% over five days and extremely extended; parabolic names can give back a lot quickly.
picks.catalyst: Memory pricing data; read-through from big-tech capex.
picks.name: Sandisk
picks.thesis: Flash memory rides the same AI storage wave as Micron; up about 375% this year and trending on WSB again.

picks.bear: Investors worry about the premium, share dilution and regulatory review. Deal overhang can weigh for months.
picks.catalyst: Deal details and analyst reactions this week.
picks.name: Marvell Technology
picks.social: Lumentum mentions spiked on WSB as the rumor spread.
picks.thesis: Dropped over 13% on reports it would buy Lumentum; the deal was confirmed today. If the market warms to the optical-networking fit, the dip could recover.

picks.bear: Guidance cut points to a PC slump; broken charts after a guide-down often keep sliding.
picks.name: Intel
picks.thesis: Plunged about 25% on weak Q4 guidance after a huge run this year. Bounce traders are circling.

picks.bear: Oil fell more than 6% today on Iran peace-talk hopes. Oil producers track crude closely.
picks.name: Permian Resources
picks.thesis: Appears on both Forbes growth and value screens: low P/E, analyst upside and solid cash flow.

picks.bear: Big run already; renewable-diesel margins are policy-sensitive, and the midterms add uncertainty.
picks.name: Darling Ingredients
picks.thesis: Up about 68% this year with analysts still seeing about 22% upside to a $34.44 consensus target. On both Forbes November lists.

picks.bear: Consumer staple with a growth multiple; a slowdown would be punished.
picks.catalyst: Steady compounding; no event this week.
picks.name: Freshpet
picks.thesis: Sales up 16% driven by volume, not price, and about 800,000 new households added. Motley Fool picks it as a growth name that can hold up in a Nasdaq correction.

picks.bear: Remittance policy and fintech competition; mid-cap volatility.
picks.name: Remitly Global
picks.thesis: Digital remittances with strong growth and target upside per Forbes' November screen.

picks.bear: Thin coverage and trading volume; small-cap pharma can swing 20% on one headline.
picks.name: Eton Pharmaceuticals
picks.thesis: Analysts project about 40% annual revenue growth and roughly 90% earnings growth; all four covering analysts rate it Buy and WallStreetZen grades it A.

regime.label: Cautious
regime.note: Nasdaq and S&P 500 fell three straight weeks; the Nasdaq dropped 2.9% Friday and 5.3% in October as AI spending drew scrutiny. Monday opened higher as oil slid on Iran talk hopes. Tuesday's midterms, Friday's jobs report and about 750 earnings reports (Apple, Palantir, AMD) make this a high-event week.
